releaseTarget.decision: passed locally with three documented, non-reachable React Router residual advisories

npm.reason: Safe React 18 / R3F 8-compatible minor update removes the vulnerable uuid@9.0.1 dependency path.
Exact patch resolves GHSA-2j2x-hqr9-3h42 while preserving the accepted v6 BrowserRouter contract.
Reviewed same-tool major update is Node 20-compatible and clears all reported Vite, esbuild, and PostCSS high/moderate paths; the package is also corrected from runtime to development scope.
Pins the already resolved compatible version exactly and corrects this build plugin from runtime to development scope.

python.reason: Fixes incomplete Vary: Cookie behavior for session access.
Fixes Private Network Access defaults and all reported case, regex-priority, and plus-normalization path matching issues.
Fixes symlink following in dotenv writer helpers.
Fixes the predictable UNIX temporary-directory vulnerability reported during the live Prompt 09A scan.

transitiveRemediations.note: Removed from the installed tree by @react-three/drei 9.122.0.

npmAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: development-only; it appeared in the baseline npm production tree because @vitejs/plugin-react was misclassified as a runtime dependency
npmAdvisories.reachability: Only the local/CI React transform and source-map pipeline invokes Babel. It is not emitted into the browser application; attacker-controlled build input was not found.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Resolve @babel/core above 7.29.0 through the reviewed plugin/tooling lockfile and move the plugin to development scope.

npmAdvisories.reachability: Only lint/config glob matching reaches this package. Public requests do not supply brace patterns, but malicious repository input could consume CI resources.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Refresh the compatible transitive lockfile resolution to at least 1.1.16.

npmAdvisories.reachability: Only lint/config glob matching reaches this package. Public requests do not supply brace patterns, but malicious repository input could trigger memory exhaustion in CI.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Refresh the compatible transitive lockfile resolution to at least 1.1.17.

npmAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: development-only; it appeared in the baseline npm production tree through the misclassified Vite dependency
npmAdvisories.reachability: The affected service is Vite's development server, not the deployed static browser bundle. No public dev-server deployment is configured.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Upgrade Vite to a compatible release resolving esbuild at 0.25.0 or newer and classify Vite as development-only.

npmAdvisories.reachability: Only tracked lint configuration is parsed; public application input is not parsed as YAML. Malicious repository YAML could still consume CI CPU.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Refresh the compatible ESLint transitive resolution beyond 4.1.1.

npmAdvisories.reachability: Only tracked lint configuration is parsed; public application input is not parsed as YAML. Malicious repository YAML could still consume CI CPU.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Refresh the compatible ESLint transitive resolution to at least 4.3.0.

npmAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: development-only; it appeared in the baseline npm production tree through the misclassified Vite dependency

npmAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: development-only; it appeared in the baseline npm production tree through the misclassified Vite dependency

npmAdvisories.reachability: Navigation runs in the browser. Existing return-route validation rejects protocol-relative and external destinations, but the compatible patch was available and required.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin react-router-dom exactly to 6.30.4 so its matching react-router dependency resolves to the patched v6 release.

npmAdvisories.reachability: No reviewed caller passes attacker-controlled destinations directly to Link or navigate. Every dynamic post-auth destination passes isSafeInternalReturnTo, which rejects backslashes, protocol-relative URLs, CR/LF, and external URLs; focused hostile-destination tests pass.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Retain the exact, otherwise patched v6 line with the tested destination allowlist until a React Router line without the newly introduced v7 high advisory can be migrated safely.
npmAdvisories.finalStatus: accepted residual; present in audit, no known exploitable application path

npmAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: runtime package; affected feature is server-side rendering only
npmAdvisories.reachability: GrapeVyne is a client-rendered Vite BrowserRouter SPA. It has no React Router server renderer, hydration-data transport, deserializeErrors call, StaticRouterProvider, or HydratedRouter path.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Retain the exact v6 BrowserRouter contract until a safe major is available; continue preventing SSR/hydration features from entering this deployment without a new review.
npmAdvisories.finalStatus: accepted residual; affected SSR deserialization feature is absent

npmAdvisories.firstFixedVersion: no patched v6 release; 7.13.0 on the v7 line
npmAdvisories.reachability: The exploit requires unsafe attacker-influenced navigation. Auth return state is constructed from the current internal pathname and all dynamic destinations pass isSafeInternalReturnTo, which rejects external, protocol-relative, backslash, CR, and LF variants. Focused tests cover these cases.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Keep the exact v6 package with the tested internal-path boundary until a v7-or-later line that resolves all router advisories is compatible and regression-proven.
npmAdvisories.finalStatus: accepted residual; present in audit, no known exploitable application path

npmAdvisories.reachability: Application source does not import uuid or call the affected v3/v5/v6 caller-supplied buffer APIs; the path nevertheless existed in the runtime tree.
npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Use the compatible @react-three/drei 9.122.0 graph, which removes uuid rather than forcing an API-incompatible transitive override.
npmAdvisories.finalStatus: resolved; uuid removed from the installed tree

npmAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: development-only; it was incorrectly declared as a runtime dependency at baseline

npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin the Node 20-compatible Vite 6.4.3 release and move it to development scope.

npmAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: development-only; it was incorrectly declared as a runtime dependency at baseline

npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin Vite 6.4.3 and move it to development scope.

npmAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: development-only; it was incorrectly declared as a runtime dependency at baseline

npmAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin Vite 6.4.3 and move it to development scope.

pythonAdvisories.reachability: The signed-session application reads session values and can sit behind a caching proxy. Existing private/no-store and Vary: Cookie controls reduce exposure, but do not replace the package fix.
pythonAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin Flask exactly to 3.1.3 and rerun session, cookie, private-cache, error-envelope, and migration coverage.

pythonAdvisories.reachability: Credentialed CORS is active for exact configured origins. The old default could approve Private Network Access for an otherwise allowed origin, so origin narrowing alone was not a package-level fix.
pythonAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Upgrade to the unified exact Flask-Cors 6.0.5 target, explicitly disable Private Network Access, and cover preflight denial.
pythonAdvisories.finalStatus: resolved at 6.0.5; PNA is explicitly disabled

pythonAdvisories.reachability: This scanner row is a withdrawn/duplicate alias of PYSEC-2024-71 rather than a second vulnerability. Its PNA behavior was reachable under the same conditions and is therefore retained rather than hidden from the row count.
pythonAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Apply the same exact Flask-Cors 6.0.5 upgrade and explicit PNA denial as the canonical record.
pythonAdvisories.finalStatus: resolved at 6.0.5; duplicate scanner row retained for accounting

pythonAdvisories.reachability: The app uses one exact-origin API policy, which reduces differential-policy impact, but case-insensitive resource matching could still select a policy for the wrong case-sensitive path.
pythonAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin Flask-Cors 6.0.5, anchor the API resource expression, and test mixed-case boundary denial.
pythonAdvisories.finalStatus: resolved at 6.0.5 with focused path-boundary regression coverage

pythonAdvisories.reachability: A single exact-origin API policy reduces the risk of a permissive longer regex outranking a restrictive one, but the vulnerable matcher remained in the runtime dependency.
pythonAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin Flask-Cors 6.0.5 and test policy precedence with anchored API and static-path controls.
pythonAdvisories.finalStatus: resolved at 6.0.5 with focused policy-precedence coverage

pythonAdvisories.reachability: The old plus-to-space normalization could select an unexpected resource policy. The app's single API policy reduced but did not remove that matcher defect.
pythonAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin Flask-Cors 6.0.5 and add plus-character and API-boundary CORS regressions.
pythonAdvisories.finalStatus: resolved at 6.0.5 with focused plus-path coverage

pythonAdvisories.reachability: The issue is local to predictable UNIX pytest temporary directories; pytest is absent from the production runtime, but developer or shared CI hosts could be affected by another local user.
pythonAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin pytest exactly to 9.0.3 and rerun the complete backend and migration suites.

pythonAdvisories.runtimeOrDevelopmentOnly: runtime package; affected writer helpers are local tooling paths
pythonAdvisories.reachability: Reviewed application code calls load_dotenv only and does not call vulnerable set_key or unset_key symlink-following writers. The exact patch was still available and required.
pythonAdvisories.proposedRemediation: Pin python-dotenv exactly to 1.2.2 and retain read-only runtime usage.

evaluatedAlternatives.reason: Although it resolves the three v6 moderate records, the live audit reports two high affected package entries through GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (RSC-mode CSRF) for react-router >=7.12.0 <8.3.0. GrapeVyne does not use RSC, but adopting a new major with a high advisory would fail the explicit release target.

The first fix for GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 requires the React Router 8.3 line, Node >=22.22, and React/React DOM >=19.2.7; no matching react-router-dom 8.3 migration was available in the evaluated graph. That would violate the Node 20 and React 18/R3F 8 compatibility anchors.
This exact patch removes the v6 protocol-relative redirect advisory and leaves only three application-unreachable moderate records, with zero high or critical entries and no framework migration.
